notes: Major disagreement on resolution claims (C5, C101-C103). LLM accepts 3.9-5.5 Å resolution with gold-standard validation as sufficient. Peer reviewers express concern about inflated resolution claims due to potential overfitting, requesting additional FSC analyses and expecting lower reported resolution.

Disagreement on de novo FrhB modeling (C6, C38, C63-C64, C114, C148). LLM finds multiple converging lines of evidence sufficient for the novel fold determination. Peer reviewers question whether map quality supports reliable ab initio modeling, requesting stronger justification given resolution concerns.

Agreement on overall architecture (C7, C8, C36). Both accept the dodecameric quaternary structure with tetrahedral symmetry forming spherical shell. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge this corrects previous models for the assembly.

Agreement on FrhA homology to group 1 hydrogenase (C43-C47). Both accept structural homology and modeling based on known counterparts. Peer reviewers implicitly accept by acknowledging two subunits have hydrogenase counterparts without raising concerns.

Partial overlap on FrhG structure (C48-C50 shared). LLM provides detailed analysis of N-terminal homology and C-terminal ferredoxin domain with gene correction. Peer reviewers accept homology-based modeling without detailed critique, but only partial claim overlap exists.

Partial agreement on FrhB as novel iron-sulfur flavoprotein (C62-C63 shared). Peer reviewers accept the identification and novelty of FrhB composition. However, they question de novo modeling quality (covered in separate pairing with R2), while LLM addresses broader structural determination claims.

Disagreement on F420 binding site identification (C9, C83-C89). LLM finds difference mapping and distance constraints provide strong evidence. Peer reviewers' concerns about overall map quality and resolution indirectly affect confidence in substrate localization, though not explicitly critiqued.

Agreement on model quality concerns (C115-C118). Both express uncertainty about model reliability. LLM notes limitations including Ramachandran outliers and borderline resolution. Peer reviewers request additional validation metrics (cross-correlation, objective FSC comparisons) to demonstrate model quality.

Minimal overlap (C9, C112 related to substrate). LLM supports complete electron transfer chain visualization. Peer reviewers' uncertainty about map quality affects confidence in detailed features, though electron transfer architecture not explicitly questioned.

Minimal overlap (C36 only). Both address cryo-EM methodology and overall architecture respectively with SUPPORTED status, but claim sets largely non-overlapping. Agreement where they intersect on structural determination.

LLM addresses electron transfer chain architecture and lack of conformational changes (C82, C98, C109) not explicitly evaluated in peer review results. These mechanistic insights appear unique to LLM analysis.

Peer reviewers accept background knowledge claims (C1-C4, C10-C32) about hydrogenases, methanogenesis, and F420 function. LLM results do not separately evaluate these established facts from literature, focusing instead on new experimental findings.
